standard.title: Hydraulically Regulated Door Closers — Specification (Fifth Revision)
standard.description: This standard specifies requirements for hydraulically regulated door closers (both fire-rated and non-fire-rated, overhead and concealed type) intended for installation on vertical-hinge doors opening to one side only, with leaf widths up to 1,600 mm and door masses up to 160 kg. It specifies physical dimensions, arm designs (including standard, parallel, and slide arms), and detailed performance testing for speed regulation, latching control, back-check damping, and delayed closing.

certification.description: Strict Statutory Mandatory Certification. Under the 'Door Fittings (Quality Control) Order' (QCO) issued by the Ministry of Commerce and Industry (DPIIT), Government of India, all hydraulically regulated door closers (overhead and concealed, fire-rated and non-fire-rated) must conform to IS 3564 : 2025 and carry the mandatory BIS Standard Mark (ISI Mark). Manufacturing, importing, distributing, or stocking non-certified door closers is a punishable statutory offense under the Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 2016. Precious metal hallmarking is completely inapplicable to industrial builders hardware components.
requirements: Each door closer body and packaged assembly must bear the BIS Standard Mark (ISI Mark) along with the manufacturer's registered licence number (CM/L) and standard reference to verify quality compliance.

Under the fifth revision, the standard specifies requirements for door closers suitable for door leaf masses up to 160 kg (previously capped at 80 kg) and leaf widths up to 1,600 mm, covering both fire-rated and non-fire-rated applications.

The door closer regulating valves must be adjusted so that the test door closes smoothly and completely from a 90° open position down to the fully closed position in a regulated manner within a time frame of 3 to 7 seconds, preventing slamming.

If latch control is provided, it must be effective over a maximum range of 15 degrees from the fully closed position and must be adjustable to ensure a smooth transition from closing to latching without slamming the door.

When fitted with a back-check function, the door closer must be capable of hydraulically cushioning or stopping the test door before it reaches the 90-degree open position to prevent wind or impact damage to surrounding structures.

If a delayed closing feature is provided, the closing time from 90° to the end of the delay zone must not be less than 20 seconds when tested at (25 ± 5)°C. The delay zone must not extend beyond the 65-degree open position, and the manual override torque must not exceed 150 Nm. After 500 cycles of testing, the delay time must remain between 10 and 30 seconds.

Mechanical efficiency must be measured during cycling using force gauges perpendicular to the door face from 0° to 4° and 88° to 92° (moving no faster than 1°/s). The efficiency is calculated as the ratio of average maximum closing force to average maximum opening force multiplied by 100, which must meet or exceed standard requirements at both the start and end of durability cycling.
